name: BOOM — Berkeley Out-of-Order Machine
description: Superscalar, out-of-order RISC-V processor written in Chisel. Originally a graduate research project, now widely used as a teaching platform for advanced microarchitecture study.

name: CVA6 (Ariane)
description: 64-bit, application-class RISC-V core capable of booting Linux. Developed at ETH Zürich's PULP Lab and now a widely adopted open-source reference for out-of-order execution research.

name: Ibex
description: Small, 32-bit RISC-V microcontroller core (RV32IMC) for energy-constrained embedded systems. Originated from ETH Zürich's zero-riscy project, now maintained under lowRISC.

name: SHAKTI Processor Family
description: India's first indigenous RISC-V processor family, developed entirely by students and researchers at IIT Madras. Spans embedded C-class cores through high-performance E-class server designs.

name: BRISC-V
description: Modular, open-source RISC-V design space exploration platform built at Brown University. Supports single-cycle, multi-cycle, and pipelined core configurations for architecture coursework.

name: OpenPiton + Ariane
description: Many-core research platform integrating the Ariane RISC-V core into Princeton's OpenPiton framework, enabling scalable multi-core architecture research across dozens of tiles.

name: Rocket Chip Generator
description: Parameterizable RISC-V SoC generator written in Chisel, originally produced by UC Berkeley students. Underpins much of the commercial and academic RISC-V ecosystem as a foundational reference design.

name: XiangShan (香山)
description: High-performance, open-source RISC-V processor developed by students at the Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences. Targets server-class performance with aggressive out-of-order pipelines.
